# Findings (auto-generated)

- Mean score 2.060 → 2.284 (+0.225). 28% of that is withdrawals removing weak papers (+0.064); 72% is reviewers actually changing ratings (+0.161).
- 6,127 of 40,544 papers (15.1%) were withdrawn; their mean initial score was 1.70 vs 2.12 for papers that stayed.
- Reviewers who joined the discussion raised their rating 29% of the time, vs 5% for reviewers who stayed silent (×5.9).
- Harsher reviewers engaged less: discussion participation was 24% for rating 1, 37% for rating 2, 46% for rating 3, 47% for rating 4.
- Share of reviews raised, by starting rating: 1 → 11.1%, 2 → 18.2%, 3 → 6.0%, 4 → 0.0%. Only 0.6% of reviews went down.
- Across 21 areas, an area's mean initial score does not predict its withdrawal rate (r = 0.24, p = 0.30), even though withdrawn papers individually scored low. The highest-withdrawal areas (vision, robotics, generative models) score above average; one guess worth checking is resubmission to a vision conference with a November deadline.
- Areas where more authors wrote rebuttals did not clearly see bigger score gains (r = 0.27, p = 0.236).
- Withdrawal rate ranges from 8% (learning theory) to 25% (applications to computer vision).
- Unlike countries, areas do differ in how much scores moved: Q = 105.1 on 20 df, p = 2e-13 (areas don't share papers, so this test is clean).
- Score change by area ranges from +0.128 (neurosymbolic & hybrid AI systems) to +0.196 (generative models).
- Among 15 countries with ≥50 open papers, score change spans +0.171 to +0.224; heterogeneity test Q = 10.4, p = 0.731 → consistent with the same bump everywhere.
- Rebuttal participation by country (top 6 by papers): China 69%, United States 79%, South Korea 82%, Hong Kong SAR China 71%, United Kingdom 80%, Germany 86%.
- Withdrawal rate by country (top 6): China 15%, United States 10%, South Korea 10%, Hong Kong SAR China 13%, United Kingdom 9%, Germany 8%.
- 178 institutions have ≥10 open papers; with a Bonferroni cut of |z| > 3.63, 0 stand out from the overall bump.
- By organization type: education initial 2.18 → change +0.200, company initial 2.23 → change +0.195, facility initial 2.16 → change +0.199.
- Caveat: country/institution tables cover 10,520 of 40,544 papers (those with an earlier preprint). Those papers started higher (2.19 vs 2.02), so they are not a random sample.
- Author comments peaked on 2026-11-18 (48,396); there were 265,321 author comments vs 54,690 reviewer comments overall (4.9 per reviewer comment).
